tools.name: list_assets
tools.description: Find the assets ChangeNOW can exchange and turn what the user said into a canonical asset id. Search by ticker, name or network, filter by network, by fiat or crypto, and by whether a fixed rate is possible. tools.name: get_asset
tools.description: Everything needed to build a swap for one asset: the canonical id, the legacy ticker used in website links, decimals, whether a memo is required and what the receiving side calls it, the address format, the token contract and the warnings to relay to the user. tools.name: quote_swap
tools.description: Ask what a swap would give, in either direction: pass amount_from to learn what the user receives, or amount_to to learn what the user must send. Returns the rate, the pair minimum and maximum, who would execute the order, and the warnings to relay. With rate_type "fixed" it also returns the rate_id

tools.name: validate_address
tools.description: Check a recipient address, and its memo when the asset needs one, against the format the network requires, before any order exists. Call this on every address the user gives. tools.name: swap_link
tools.description: Build a changenow.io link with the pair, the amount, the recipient address and the memo already filled in, so the user checks the numbers on the real page and presses Confirm themselves. tools.name: create_swap
tools.description: Create a real swap order and return the deposit address the user has to send funds to. This call moves no money by itself, but the order is real: it exists in support, it can expire, and a fixed rate is locked against it. tools.name: check_swap_status
tools.description: Follow an existing order by id: where it stands, what the deposit and payout amounts turned out to be, the transaction hashes, and a plain-language explanation of what the current stage means and what happens next. Use it after create_swap, and again whenever the user asks where their swap is.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "create_swap" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.
